text:
Maya: ran the long-context benchmark overnight, saw persistent resident growth instead of settling after repeated compaction cycles. Expected ~15GB steady; observed ~26GB after ~9 hours.
Simon: yikes. command + node spec?
Maya: ```
# node: perf-rt-gpu-8 equiv
./bench_longctx --model llama-2-13b --tokens 1.2e9 --concurrency 6 \n  --kv-page-size=4096 --compaction-interval=60s --reuse-policy=aggressive
```
Maya: node uses jemalloc with per-thread arenas and persistent-kv. compaction runs every minute per logs but reclaimed bytes are much smaller than freed bytes.
Cheng: can you dump smaps or pmap near the end? want anon vs mmapped fractions.
Maya: short summary:
PID MemRSS Anon Mmap
33421 26.1G 19.4G 5.9G
# host shows many tiny mmaps ~4K and growing anon pages
Nora: smells like fragmentation and arena-held extents. did you capture heap/profile samples while RSS climbed?
Maya: grabbed offcpu + heap snapshots. flame excerpt:
kv::alloc_small
kv::page_table::hold_extent
kv::compaction::backoff
io::submit_batch
Simon: "hold_extent" + compaction backoff indicates free extents aren't being coalesced or handed back to the allocator global pool. per-thread arenas could be hoarding.
Cheng: also compaction throttle could be delaying reclamation until it's too late, producing the observed RSS ramp.
Maya: p95 latency increased ~15ms after a few hours, p50 unchanged. throughput nominal.
Maya: minimal repro (short run):
./bench_longctx --model test-small --tokens 6e7 --concurrency 4 \n  --kv-page-size=4096 --compaction-interval=10s --reuse-policy=aggressive
# within ~30m RSS climbs and compaction logs show freed << reclaimed
Simon: try running with MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,oversize_threshold:8 and capture jemalloc stats.
Maya: snapshot highlights: allocated: 7.8G, resident: 10.8G, retained: 11.6G (retained > allocated). many small dirty extents in arenas.
Nora: retained > allocated is classic arena retention. fragmentation + rounding for small allocations will keep pages resident even after free.
Cheng: mitigation ideas: call mallctl to purge arenas during compaction, coalesce freed small extents in kv allocator before returning, or reduce compaction deferral under steady workloads.
Simon: can you try a quick hack to purge arenas at the end of compaction and measure impact?
Maya: did a local patch that advances epoch then calls arena purge for each arena. 1h run: peak RSS fell to ~17.5GB and the ramp disappeared.
Maya: pseudocode change:
# at end of compaction cycle
mallctl("epoch", ...);
for each arena: mallctl("arena.%d.purge", ...);
Cheng: good win. what's the perf tradeoff? purge can block and spike CPU.
Maya: CPU delta ~+3% overall during purge windows, p95 latency unchanged, throughput steady. seems acceptable on dedicated perf nodes but could be problematic on mixed traffic hosts.
Nora: propose a selective purge heuristic: only purge arenas where retained/allocated ratio > 1.15 and only when qps below threshold. also consider async or incremental purge to avoid large pauses.
Simon: proposed action items:
1) Maya: add a focused bench that alternates cold/warm long-context patterns to reproduce fragmentation deterministically (PR).
2) Cheng: run fleet comparison (purge on vs off) and collect jemalloc stats + smaps.
3) Nora: design selective purge policy + safety gates (no synchronous purge >X qps).
4) bench-bot/CI: add regression that asserts RSS growth <20% over 6h for a toy long-context workload.
Maya: uploaded artifacts and snapshots to perf store: https://perf.redwood/s3/kv-retain-192345 (link in issue).
bench-bot: scheduled job 2024-11-08T04:00:00Z -> perf/longctx/kv-retain-regress-ci
Simon: I'll open a tracking issue with logs and label infra for jemalloc tuning. assign to Nora for selective purge design.
Nora: will draft a short design doc and post to #eng-runtime by EOD with safety knobs and metric checks.
Maya: thanks all :thumbsup: aiming to gate a regression test before the next release.
Cheng: will attach pprof heap + perf.data to the issue after fleet runs complete.
